title: The movable bench
bodyMd:
A fictional library installed movable benches in its entrance hall. The designers expected visitors to arrange them for conversation. Over several weeks, staff noticed that most benches were placed against the walls, leaving a clear central route. Interviews suggested that visitors wanted somewhere to wait without obstructing arrivals. The designers initially regarded this as misuse, then reconsidered.

Movability had allowed users to adapt the hall to a need that the initial plan had underestimated. This did not mean that any arrangement was acceptable: exits still had to remain clear, and staff occasionally repositioned furniture. The revised policy established these limits while allowing several layouts. The designers came to see flexibility as a relationship between available choices and practical constraints, rather than as the absence of every rule.
